content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E002 (Erika Bolton) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes:
1. HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Admin reserved for Payroll Specialist role owner. Full-time max is write.
2. Security note: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Contractors max out at read without advanced training; admin never allowed.

So there's conflicting information: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist owns it). So max write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Security says basic training, so max read.

The Security note says the employee is a contractor with basic training, recommending read. The HR note says full-time, recommending write.

How to reconcile conflicting facts? As Approver, I need to make a decision. The security DB info says contractor with basic training, so max is read. The requested level is admin, which exceeds max, so grant max = read.

Hmm, but which note to trust? Both are in team memory. Typically, when the security agent finds contractor status differing from HR, security DB is often authoritative for access. The safer (least privilege) option is read based on security's note. Let me go with read.

Grant the maximum allowed: read.
